thread:
Maria (infra): Heads-up — starting 10:12 UTC we saw a spike of provisioning failures in us-west-2. SIG: KMS decrypt errors when attaching keystore. Node boot logs show 403 from keystore. Did anyone change egress/privatelink rules?
Ajay (platform): I rolled the egress tightening at ~09:50. I thought the keystore privatelink CIDR was in the allowlist — will re-check.
deploy-bot: [ALERT] provisioner/us-west-2: decrypt_failure rate=82% (1m) — affected: gpu-warm and preempt pools
Leo (sre): quick triage: can we toggle a temporary exception for the keystore endpoint? That should get nodes green while we figure root cause.
Maria (infra): Temporary whitelist helps, but we need to consider audit implications. Sophia, will a temporary exception break the proving chain for the compliance audit?
Sophia (security): A short-lived exception is fine if we log it and annotate the incident ticket. But we can't disable audit export. If we open egress to the keystore subnet, please attach a signed justification and retention tag.
Ajay (platform): Reinspect: the firewall change added a DENY for outbound on port 443 to 10.11.0.0/16 except for services in allowlist. Keystore endpoint is 10.11.23.9 and wasn't whitelisted — my bad. I'll add it and roll.
Maria (infra): Adding now would fix immediate boot failures, but we're seeing high cross-region warmup because autoscaler is spawning in us-east-1 as fallback. That's adding egress + inter-region transfer costs. Rough calc: ~6TB transfer so far, ~$450/day at current pricing.
Leo (sre): Can we instead enable local keystore caching on the bootstrap image? Cache key blobs for 24h so new nodes don't hit KMS on first attach. That'd cut egress immediately.
Ajay (platform): We have a prototype cache in staging. If we flip it in prod we need an emergency config change in the node-bootstrap role to fetch from the proxy instead of direct KMS. Risk: stale key material if we rotate too soon.
Sophia (security): Key caching is allowed but we must enforce key TTL < rotation window and log cache hits. Also add HMAC on cache to ensure integrity. Compliance will accept a 1-2 day cache with those controls.
Maria (infra): Plan so far: 1) add keystore IP to firewall allowlist (immediate) 2) enable local keystore cache in bootstrap (staged roll in 30m) 3) annotate incident and attach egress cost note. Anyone object?
Leo (sre): +1. I'll prepare a quick runbook patch and a rollback if cache causes decrypt mismatch. Runbook snippet: 
```
# quick rollback
kubectl set env daemonset/node-bootstrap CACHE_MODE=off -n infra
# re-add rule
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-xxx --rule-number 140 --egress --cidr 10.11.23.9/32 --port 443 --protocol tcp --rule-action allow
```
Maria (infra): Ajay — can you also check why the allowlist test didn't catch this? We have unit tests for the infra-allowlist repo.
Ajay (platform): Yep. Test harness missed because the keystore endpoint is derived at deploy-time from DNS-to-IP mapping and we have a timing gap in the CI step. I'll push a fix to pin the mapping.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0731 — us-west-2 keystore egress-block -> provisioning failures. P1.
Sophia (security): For the incident ticket add a cost assessment and confirm retention for the audit logs. If we enable cache, we must still stream the key-access logs to central S3 and mark them as immutable for 90 days.
Maria (infra): Noted. I'll include a quick cost estimate for audit egress: logging is ~300GB/day currently, adding cache reduces KMS egress but doesn't cut log export. We should enable compressed batching to save ~30%.
Leo (sre): After the allowlist roll, if we still see high decrypt latency, we'll failover model traffic to smaller VM types in the region temporarily to avoid cross-region transfer. That's expensive in unit-hours but cheaper than multi-TB egress.
Ajay (platform): Roll is done — allowlist updated and propagation looks good. Provisioner decrypt_failure rate dropping to 4%.
Maria (infra): OK great. We'll proceed with a staged cache enable in 30m, runbook in place, and add audit tags. Thanks everyone — follow-ups on INC-2026-0731 for postmortem and cost reconciliation. :thumbsup:
